summary.intent: Continue and complete GSD Phase 70.1 (rotation read-plane durability and crash-resume soundness) execution: land 13 plans across 7 waves via parallel worktrees, get the D-16 desktop-e2e human acceptance checkpoint green on macOS/Linux/Windows, run phase verification, then execute the full /ship-phase 70.1 flow (verify/secure/validate/simplify/SDK-E2E/CodeRabbit/ship/resolve-reviews) to open and prepare PR #598 for merge.
summary.outcome: Phase 70.1 fully executed and shipped: all 13 plans merged, three genuine product bugs found and fixed (depth-3 decrypt-before-dirtiness-check ordering bug in both engines, JsonSidecarFloorStore multi-writer race, and a scope-exit revocation-bypass + double-publish bug caught by the D-16 acceptance test), D-16 went green on all three platforms, verification/security/nyquist/simplify/SDK-E2E gates all passed, CodeRabbit findings triaged (2 more real bugs fixed: fail-open child-list override causing silent data loss, and a TS/Rust parity gap where TS immediately GC'd ECIES checkpoints instead of deferring until durable republish), and PR #598 was opened with all fixes committed, pending final CI confirmation.

code.finding: JsonSidecarFloorStore::new() previously built its own independent Arc<Mutex<()>> per instance even when multiple instances pointed at the same sidecar path, causing a rename-race (ENOENT) when e.g. rotation_checkpoint_store and high_water stores wrote concurrently; fixed via a process-global path-keyed lock registry (shared_lock_for).

repairDirtyNode called deleteWrappedKey (GC of the ECIES checkpoint) immediately after updating a parent's in-memory mirror, even when the parent still had other pending dirty children (no republish yet) — a crash in that window permanently loses the checkpoint. The Rust twin (engine.rs) already deferred GC via pending_checkpoint_node_ids until the batched republish commits; TS lacked this and had to be ported to match.

build_scope_exit_child_override failed OPEN per-child (child-not-found → continue; build_child_refs error → warn+skip) unlike its fail-closed sibling build_folder_metadata, and since the override REPLACES the published child list wholesale, a transiently-missing sibling would be silently dropped from the folder — orphaning it with no EIO.

rotate_read_on_scope_exit originally matched Ok(_) and discarded the RotateReadResult without refreshing the grant-root inode's in-memory read_key, so a subsequent relink resealed under the stale old key and republished last — the newest IPNS record ended up old-key-sealed, letting a revoked recipient still decrypt it (revocation bypass).

CipherBoxFS::refresh_sent_shares had zero call sites on the desktop mount lifecycle; the D-15a fail-closed fix meant every real-mount delete/rename returned EIO because sent_shares stayed non-authoritative. Fixed with a bounded mount-init refresh + 30s periodic background refresh.

Publish-queue drain (drain_upload_completions/flush_publish_queue) is edge-triggered only from FUSE op handlers with no wall-clock backstop; on macOS FUSE-T, handle_release is deferred ~40s past when a test/client stops touching the mount, so a queued parent republish never fires. Fixed with an idle-mount background pump thread (2s interval, unique never-cached filenames) plus a harness-side nudge.

workflow: When forking multiple git worktrees in parallel, dispatch each `git worktree add` in its own message/tool call — simultaneous adds race on .git/config.lock.
Scope `cargo fmt` to the specific crate (`-p <crate>`) not `--all` — workspace-wide fmt reformats unrelated files and strands uncommitted drift that blocks worktree merges.
This repo's CI does not run `cargo fmt --check`, so local `cargo fmt` runs can introduce unnecessary version-skew churn against already-passing committed code — verify before applying broad fmt.

Cross-package dist staleness is a real trap: after changing sdk-core in one wave, downstream consumer packages (sdk) must be rebuilt before their vitest suite reflects the change, or tests fail with misleading errors.

sdk-e2e requires sourcing apps/api/.env into the shell (`set -a; . ./.env; set +a`) before running vitest — the harness has no built-in dotenv loader, so SDK_E2E_SECRET silently falls back to a default and causes a 401.

rust-analyzer diagnostics (dead_code, E0063, unresolved imports) go stale mid-edit and should be re-verified with an authoritative `cargo check`/`cargo test` before trusting them, especially when multiple agents/background builds are touching the same crate.
Windows CI exit code -1073741502 (0xC0000142 STATUS_DLL_INIT_FAILED) is a known transient runner flake at process startup, not a code issue — safe to just re-run the failed job.
GSD's commit helper occasionally reports 'commit_failed' as a false negative when lint-staged is just slow; verify via `git log --oneline -1` rather than retrying blindly.
`gh run rerun --failed` can print a spurious 'cannot be rerun' message while actually working — confirm via `gh run view` status rather than trusting the CLI's own message.

Two rust-analyzer processes each consuming ~5.5GB can indicate an orphaned editor/session pointed at a stale worktree whose directory no longer exists on disk — check each PID's parent and cwd before assuming it's normal workspace overhead.

friction: Canary-first single-plan dispatch was flagged by the user as not matching their explicit 'all 4 plans concurrently' request — required correcting the approach mid-wave.
cleanup-wave merge blocked on worktree_dirty due to an unscoped `cargo fmt --all` leaving out-of-scope drift uncommitted in a worktree.
Stale dist (sdk-core changed but sdk not rebuilt) produced 3 false-failing tests in Wave 3's post-merge gate, requiring investigation before recognizing it as staleness rather than a regression.

D-16 desktop-e2e required many iterative debug/fix/CI-round-trip cycles (macOS setup timeout, Windows +2 count, revocation bypass, double-publish) before going green on all three platforms — each real-mount CI run costs ~15-40 minutes.

A live idle-mount validation of the macOS publish-pump fix could not be performed reliably on the interactive dev machine because Spotlight/Finder generate spontaneous FUSE ops that mask the exact bug being fixed — had to defer to CI as the only valid arbiter.

Ship-phase Step 5 (SDK E2E gate) surfaced 2 unrelated tee-republish test failures caused by a local-stack precondition (TEE worker not initialized) that had to be diagnosed and classified as out-of-scope before proceeding.

Committing several files together hit the 120s Bash timeout partway through due to slow lint-staged (eslint+prettier) hooks, requiring a check of partial commit state and a longer timeout for the remainder.

CodeRabbit findings required careful adversarial verification since some were partially wrong (e.g. finding 6's 'missing-parent' framing was unreachable, though the underlying per-child fail-open was real) or fully refuted (finding 3's client key-borrow claim, finding 4's get_wrapped_key already-Zeroizing claim).
Two orphaned rust-analyzer/claude-code processes from a stale Phase-69 worktree (already deleted from disk) were silently leaking ~5.4GB of RAM for ~3 days.
open_items: WinFsp handle_rename ungated-dest D-15d parity gap — tracked in 2026-07-08-winfsp-d15d-gate-ordering-parity.md.

ROT-04: desktop query_grants_rooted_at is a no-op, so scope-exit rotation de-authorizes all recipients rather than selectively re-minting inner grants — tracked in 2026-07-08-desktop-query-grants-rooted-at-remint-noop.md.

macOS FUSE-T read-side sync invalidation gap causing cross-client-sync Test 5 and Test 7 to soft-skip on macOS (FUSE-T ignores inval_inode, SMB cache serves stale content) — tracked in 2026-07-09-macos-fuse-t-cross-client-sync-invalidation.md; explicitly distinct from and not fixed by the phase's write-side publish-pump.

Minor: queue.rs has a duplicated 8-line floor-sidecar-skip guard in two scan loops (load_all_for_vault and gc_failed_entries) — flagged by simplify review as low-value, deferred rather than refactored.
